answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is by binding each agent to a unique economic stake that cannot be copied. Every new agent must lock collateral before acting, and misbehavior slashes it, so flooding the network with fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Think of each honest agent as a vertex in a web of trust — the more sybils try to join, the more the sparrow signals danger in the meadow, and the cost of attack rises faster than any reward.
